title: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
authors: Zheyu Wu, Daniel Shaffer, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, Mengmeng Long, Hanyi Chen, Andrej Cabala, Theodore I. Weinberger, Maurice Bal, Steffen Wiedmann, Dave Graf, Vladimir Sechovský, Michal Vališka, F. Malte Grosche, Alex Levchenko, Alexander G. Eaton
abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.
summary: This work reports a large superconducting diode effect in UTe2, arguing that this non-reciprocal transport is an intrinsic signature of spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking. By confining the SDE to a specific magnetic/superconducting phase coexistence region, the authors strongly suggest the formation of a nonuniform, finite-momentum Cooper pair state characteristic of an FFLO phase.
main_problem: To determine if the large superconducting diode effect (SDE) observed in UTe2 indicates spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking (ISB) accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing, rather than being due to extrinsic effects like vortex pinning asymmetries.
main_result: The non-reciprocal transport (SDE) is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state, strongly suggesting an intrinsic origin linked to spontaneous ISB and nonuniform triplet pairing.
method: The study combines experimental measurements of SDE and resistivity ($ho(H)$) with theoretical modeling using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau (GL) theory.
model_or_system: The physical system is the heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe2. The theoretical framework involves an extended GL theory describing the interplay between magnetic order ($\mathbf{M}$) and superconducting order ($\Delta$), which can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.
key_observables: Superconducting Diode Effect (SDE) efficiency ($\eta$), electrical resistivity ($ho$), and the coexistence region between the SC2 and Polarized Paramagnetic (PPM) states.
important_parameters: High magnetic field strength ($\mu_0H = 33.6 	ext{ T}$), the narrow field regime of phase coexistence, and the magnitude of the diode efficiency (up to 33%).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the confinement of the SDE to a specific phase overlap rules out purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries, pointing toward an intrinsic mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $ho(H)$ dependence, the $V(J)$ characteristics showing polarity dependence, and the phase diagram mapping out the narrow region where the SDE is observed.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the SDE as a probe for ISB, presents experimental evidence showing the SDE is localized to a specific SC2/PPM coexistence region, and uses GL theory to model this confinement as evidence for an intrinsic, nonuniform FFLO state.
why_interesting: The connection between non-equilibrium transport phenomena (SDE) and intrinsic pairing symmetries (FFLO/ISB) in a strongly correlated material like UTe2 provides a powerful experimental diagnostic tool for exotic superconducting states.
